title: Philippines’ Bea Millan-Windorski finishes 3rd runner-up at Miss Universe 2026
summary: The 24-year-old stunner from La Union achieves the same finish as her predecessor, Ahtisa Manalo of Quezon, at Miss Universe

blocks.text: LA UNION STUNNER. Bea Millan-Windorski finishes in the top five at Miss Universe 2026.
Seven Barretto via Bea Millan-Windorski's Instagram
The 24-year-old stunner from La Union achieves the same finish as her predecessor, Ahtisa Manalo of Quezon, at Miss Universe
MANILA, Philippines – The Philippines’ bet Bea Millan-Windorski finished third runner-up at the 75th Miss Universe in Puerto Rico on Wednesday, November 25 (Manila time).

Puerto Rico’s Jennifer Barreto took home the title of Miss Universe 2026, and was crowned by her predecessor, Fátima Bosch of Mexico, during the coronation night at the José Miguel Agrelot Coliseum, San Juan.
Dominican Republic’s Melissa Núñez settled for first runner-up, while Venezuela’s Clara Vega finished second runner-up. Georgia Waddington of New Zealand secured fourth runner-up.
The 24-year-old Filipina had hoped to bring home the country’s fifth Miss Universe crown, following Catriona Gray (2018), Pia Wurtzbach (2015), Margarita Moran (1973), and Gloria Diaz (1969).

Windorski, who is of Filipino and American descent, represented La Union in Miss Universe Philippines 2026. A pageant veteran, she represented the US at Miss Earth 2024, where she was named Miss Earth-Water.

In 2024, she earned her bachelor’s degree at the University of Wisconsin-Madison College of Letters and Science, where she was able to hone in on her advocacy for Filipino heritage and environmental rights.
True to her advocacy, she focused on the environment in answering the pageant’s final question: “What does the world need most from its leaders right now?”
“As someone who has been an environmentalist my whole life, I wish that our world leaders would listen to nature and realize that we have much to learn,” Windorski said.

“I volunteered with sea turtles for the past 10 years, and while we’ve often heard of crab mentality or tearing one another down, turtle mentality is the opposite. The strongest sea turtle hatchlings actually stay behind in the nest to help their weaker brothers and sisters out and into the sea. I wish that our world leaders would embrace the same mentality.”
Windorski’s ranking comes just a year after Ahtisa Manalo of Quezon also finished third runner-up in last year’s edition. – Rappler.com
